questions.stem: A convex lens of focal length 15 cm forms a sharp real image of a burning candle on a screen. The lower half of the lens is now covered with an opaque black cardboard sheet. Explain with physical ray principles what happens to the image on the screen.

options.text: The top half of the candle flame disappears completely from the screen.
The complete image is still formed, but its brightness (intensity) is reduced by half.
The image flips upside down again because rays invert twice.

questions.authoritative_solution: Every point on an illuminated object emits rays across the entire lens aperture. The unobstructed upper half receives rays from all points of the candle, forming the complete image with approximately 50% reduced luminous intensity.
sample_misconception_responses: Lower half is covered so light cannot pass through bottom; only top half of flame appears.
Half the image disappears because half the glass is blocked.
sample_correct_responses: The complete image remains intact because rays from every point of the candle still pass through the open upper half, but the image becomes dimmer.
sample_slip_responses: Full image remains, but focal length changes from 15 cm to 7.5 cm.

questions.stem: An object of height 5 cm is placed at a distance of 20 cm in front of a concave mirror having a radius of curvature of 30 cm. Using the New Cartesian Sign Convention, calculate the position (v) of the image.

options.text: v = +60 cm (virtual and erect)
v = -60 cm (real and inverted)
v = -8.57 cm (calculation sign slip)

questions.authoritative_solution: By Cartesian sign convention: u = -20 cm, f = -15 cm. Mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u => 1/v = 1/(-15) - 1/(-20) = -1/60 => v = -60 cm.
sample_misconception_responses: Formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u | Given: u = +20 cm, f = +15 cm | Working: 1/v = 1/15 - 1/20 = 1/60 => v = +60 | Unit: cm
sample_correct_responses: Formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u | Given: u = -20 cm, f = -15 cm | Working: 1/v = 1/(-15) - 1/(-20) = -1/60 => v = -60 | Unit: cm

questions.stem: A student looks into a plane mirror and observes their reflection. Which statement correctly describes why the image is classified as virtual in physics?

options.text: Rays physically penetrate through the glass backing and converge behind the mirror.
Reflected rays diverge from the mirror surface; when traced backward along sightlines, they appear to intersect behind the mirror where no actual light exists.
The image is virtual only because no physical screen has been placed behind the silver coating.

questions.authoritative_solution: A virtual image is formed when diverging rays only appear to intersect when extended backward. No light physically passes behind the plane mirror.
sample_misconception_responses: Light penetrates through the mirror and focuses behind the glass.
sample_correct_responses: Diverging reflected rays appear to meet behind mirror when traced backwards.
sample_slip_responses: Image is virtual because mirror has negative focal length.

questions.stem: A narrow ray of yellow light passes obliquely from air into a rectangular parallel-faced glass slab. What is the orientation of the emergent ray relative to the incident ray?

options.text: The emergent ray is permanently bent towards the normal at an angle of 30 degrees.
The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray, shifted sideways by lateral displacement.
The emergent ray splits into seven spectral colors inside the slab.

questions.authoritative_solution: At parallel boundaries, angle of emergence equals angle of incidence (i = e). The ray emerges parallel to its incident direction with a perpendicular lateral shift.
sample_misconception_responses: The ray stays deviated at an angle like in a prism.
sample_correct_responses: Emergent ray is parallel to incident ray but laterally displaced.
sample_slip_responses: Lateral shift is zero because glass cancels refraction.

questions.stem: A convex lens of focal length 15 cm has an object placed at a distance of 30 cm in front of it. Using the Lens Formula, calculate the image distance (v).

options.text: v = -10 cm (using mirror formula by mistake)
v = +30 cm (real, inverted, same size at 2F)
v = +10 cm (sign convention error)

questions.authoritative_solution: Lens formula: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u => 1/v = 1/15 + 1/(-30) = 1/30 => v = +30 cm. Image is formed at 2F on the other side.
sample_correct_responses: Formula: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u | Given: u = -30 cm, f = +15 cm | Working: 1/v = 1/15 + 1/(-30) = 1/30 => v = +30 | Unit: cm
sample_slip_responses: Formula: 1/f = 1/v - 1/u | Given: u = +30 cm, f = +15 cm | Working: 1/v = 1/15 + 1/30 = 3/30 => v = 10 | Unit: cm

questions.stem: A convex lens projects a sharp real image of an object onto a cardboard screen. If the screen is abruptly removed, explain whether the real image still exists in space at that location.

options.text: The image disappears completely because images only exist when painted onto a physical screen.
The real image still exists in empty space at that exact focal plane (aerial image) because light rays continue to intersect there.
The image immediately converts into a virtual image located inside the glass.

questions.authoritative_solution: A real image is formed by the spatial intersection of converging rays. The screen merely scatters light diffusely so observers can view it; the aerial image exists in space independently of the screen.
sample_misconception_responses: Without the screen there is no surface, so the image cannot exist.
sample_correct_responses: The aerial image still exists in space at that plane because converging rays intersect there whether a screen is present or not.
sample_slip_responses: The image exists but focal length doubles without a screen.

questions.stem: The absolute refractive index of a glass medium is 1.5. If the speed of light in vacuum is 3 * 10^8 m/s, what is the speed of light in this glass?

options.text: 4.5 * 10^8 m/s (multiplied by refractive index)
1.5 * 10^8 m/s (speed equals refractive index constant)

questions.authoritative_solution: Refractive index n = c / v => v = c / n = (3 * 10^8 m/s) / 1.5 = 2.0 * 10^8 m/s.
sample_misconception_responses: Light speeds up in denser glass so v = c * n = 4.5 * 10^8 m/s.
sample_slip_responses: v = 1.5e8 m/s due to division slip.

questions.stem: Find the power of a concave lens having a focal length of 2 meters.

options.text: P = +0.5 D (concave lens treated as positive)
P = -0.5 D (P = 1/f with f = -2 m)
P = -2.0 D (confusing focal length with dioptre)

numerical_meta.given: f = -2 m (concave lens focal length is negative)

questions.authoritative_solution: Power P = 1 / f(in meters). For a concave lens, focal length is negative: f = -2 m. Hence, P = 1 / (-2) = -0.5 D (Dioptre).
sample_misconception_responses: Formula: P = 1 / f | Given: f = +2 m | Working: P = 1 / 2 = +0.5 | Unit: D
sample_correct_responses: Formula: P = 1 / f (in meters) | Given: f = -2 m (concave) | Working: P = 1 / (-2) = -0.5 | Unit: D
sample_slip_responses: Formula: P = f | Given: f = -2 m | Working: P = -2 | Unit: D

questions.stem: Why are convex mirrors preferred as rear-view (wing) mirrors in automobiles?

options.text: They produce magnified real images of distant vehicles on the driver eyes.
They always produce an erect, diminished virtual image and have a significantly wider field of view because they are curved outwards.
They invert the image so the driver can see behind the car upside down.

questions.authoritative_solution: Convex mirrors always give an erect though diminished virtual image. Since they curve outward, they provide a much wider field of view than a plane mirror.
sample_misconception_responses: Convex mirrors magnify cars so they look closer.
sample_correct_responses: Convex mirrors provide wider field of view and always form erect diminished images.
sample_slip_responses: Convex mirrors form inverted images at night.

questions.stem: A lemon kept in water inside a cylindrical glass tumbler appears to be significantly bigger than its actual size when viewed from the sides. Explain the physical optical cause.

options.text: The glass tumbler chemically expands the lemon cells when submerged in liquid.
Light rays from the lemon refract away from the normal when passing from water to air through the curved glass cylinder, which acts as a cylindrical magnifying lens.
Water particles reflect light back onto the lemon, creating an optical double reflection.

questions.authoritative_solution: Light travels from denser water to rarer air, bending away from the normal. The curved outer surface of the cylindrical tumbler behaves as a convex cylindrical lens, causing virtual magnification.
sample_misconception_responses: Water reflects light so the lemon looks doubled in size.
sample_correct_responses: Light refracts from denser water to rarer air at the curved cylindrical interface, which acts like a magnifying lens.
sample_slip_responses: Lemon looks bigger because focal length of water is zero.
